stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $p = u : \mathcal{C} \to \textit{Sets}$
be a functor. If the category of neighbourhoods of $p$ is
cofiltered, then the stalk functor (\ref{equation-stalk})
is left exact.
hypotheses:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Let $p = u : \mathcal{C} \to \textit{Sets}$
be a functor. If the category of neighbourhoods of $p$ is
cofiltered,
conclusions:
the stalk functor (\ref{equation-stalk})
is left exact.

reason: Presheaf limits compute sheaf limits; the stalk is the filtered colimit over the opposite of the neighbourhood category. Filtered colimits commute with finite limits in Sets, giving left exactness.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Assume that $\mathcal{C}$ has
a final object $X$ and fibred products.
Let $p = u : \mathcal{C} \to \textit{Sets}$ be a functor such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $u(X)$ is a singleton set, and
\item for every pair of morphisms $U \to W$ and $V \to W$ with
the same target the map
$u(U \times_W V) \to u(U) \times_{u(W)} u(V)$ is bijective.
\end{enumerate}
Then the the category of neighbourhoods of $p$ is cofiltered
and consequently the stalk functor $\Sh(\mathcal{C}) \to \textit{Sets}$,
$\mathcal{F} \to \mathcal{F}_p$ commutes with finite limits.

Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a site. Assume that $\mathcal{C}$ has

Let $p = u : \mathcal{C} \to \textit{Sets}$ be a functor such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $u(X)$ is a singleton set, and
\item for every pair of morphisms $U \to W$ and $V \to W$ with
the same target the map
$u(U \times_W V) \to u(U) \times_{u(W)} u(V)$ is bijective.
\end{enumerate}
conclusions:
the the category of neighbourhoods of $p$ is cofiltered
and consequently the stalk functor $\Sh(\mathcal{C}) \to \textit{Sets}$,

reason: The singleton value at a final object makes neighbourhoods nonempty; the functor's fibre-product preservation supplies common refinements, and preservation of their equalizers supplies equalization of parallel neighbourhood arrows. This establishes cofilteredness, hence the previous stalk left-exactness lemma.
